hits.text: The older I get, the more I realize that the single greatest challenge for any ambitious person is eliminating the guilt associated with free time and rest.
hits.full_text: The older I get, the more I realize that the single greatest challenge for any ambitious person is eliminating the guilt associated with free time and rest.
hits.hook: SahilBloom: greatest challenge is dropping guilt about free time and rest (best brand fit today)
hits.draft_en:
I used to treat free time like something I had to earn.

Finish the list, then sit down. Clear the inbox, then rest. The list never ends, so the sitting never starts.

I'm trying something smaller: put the pen down on purpose. Ten quiet minutes. No apology attached.
hits.video_tip: 15 seconds, overhead on textured cream paper, window light, room sound only. A phone is placed face-down beside a closed notebook. A hand uncaps a fountain pen, opens to a blank page, writes nothing for a few beats, then one short line. No face. Last frame text: 'Ten quiet minutes.'

hits.name: James Clear
hits.media_note: text-only; replies limited to mentioned users
hits.text: Your best performances will come when you are working in a way that is a full expression of you. The work becomes a natural display of your personality. This is…
hits.full_text: Your best performances will come when you are working in a way that is a full expression of you. The work becomes a natural display of your personality. This is when you not only get better results, but also love the activity — because in doing the craft, you feel alive.
hits.hook: JamesClear: best work is a full expression of you; craft that feels alive (replies locked; post or quote angle)
hits.draft_en:
The work that feels most like me is usually the slowest to show.

A page in ink. A small product decision. A homepage that still says almost live.

I'd rather build that way than force a version that looks busy and feels wrong.
hits.video_tip: 12 seconds, same desk, no face, no music. Hand writes one short line in a notebook, underlines nothing, caps the pen. Last frame text: 'Feels like me.'

reply_ideas.reply_text: This one lands. I kept treating rest like a prize for finishing the list. The list never ends. Ten quiet minutes with no apology attached has been a better experiment.
Free time used to feel like I was falling behind. I'm learning it can just be part of the workday, same as the pen and the page.
Six months still sounds short until week three, when nothing looks different yet. That's the week I try to plan for. Small enough to keep doing when it's boring.
"Deal with the two feet right in front of you" is still the part I need. The big plan gets loud fast. Two feet, I can manage.
